chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said: Muqatil ibn Sulayman narrated to me that I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both),

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean,' so he (AS) replied, 'He is equal in distance to everything, so there is no thing closer to Him than another thing.'

key_terms.أَقْرَبَ إِلَيْهِ: Closer to Him, referring to spatial or ontological proximity
key_terms.اسْتَوَى: He was firm/established, referring to divine attribute
key_terms.الرَّحْمَنُ: The Most Compassionate, a divine name
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne, often symbolizing divine authority or dominion
key_terms.مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: From/equal to every thing, indicating uniformity in distance

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah is described as 'firm on the Throne'?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'Istawa' not as physical ascent or location, but as divine sovereignty and equality of distance from creation, a view central to the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* (divine unity) against anthropomorphism. This explanation aligns with the Mu'tazili-influenced rationalist tradition often cited by al-Saduq to affirm that Allah is beyond spatial dimensions (*Jism* and *Huduth*). The phrase 'no thing is closer to Him than another' emphasizes His transcendence (*Tanzih*) over directional or locational attributes.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil said: `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub that Maqatil ibn Sulayman related to me that I asked Ja`far ibn Muhammad (AS)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean, so he (AS) replied, “He is equal in distance to everything. Therefore, He is not closer to one thing than to another.”
